papers.abstract: Abstract Treatment options for patients with immunoglobulin light chain (AL) amyloidosis and advanced cardiac involvement remain limited. The prospective phase 2 European Myeloma Network 22 trial included patients with previously untreated AL amyloidosis, measurable hematologic disease, and Mayo2004/European cardiac stage IIIB disease to receive daratumumab monotherapy at the standard dose and schedule for up to 2 years (28-day cycles); patients with inadequate response after 3 cycles could additionally receive weekly bortezomib and dexamethasone. The primary end point was 6-month overall survival (OS) rate. Of 40 patients enrolled, 10 (25.0%) received additional treatment with bortezomib and dexamethasone. The 6-month OS rate was 65% (95% confidence interval, 48.2-77.6), and median OS was 10.4 months. The best hematologic response rate (partial response or better) up to 6 months was 75% (very good partial response or better, 47.5%; complete response, 12.5%), with the median time to first and best hematologic response being 1 week and 2.3 months, respectively. Cardiac response rate at 6 months was 30%. Common serious adverse events were cardiac failure (25%), sudden cardiac death (10%), and acute kidney injury (7.5%). The patients’ quality of life remained stable throughout the trial treatment and observation. In patients with high-risk, advanced (stage IIIB) AL amyloidosis, daratumumab monotherapy was feasible and well tolerated, achieving rapid hematologic responses and associated with prolonged survival relative to historical cohorts. Cardiac response rates at 6 months were significant, considering advanced cardiac disease. These findings support daratumumab as the backbone of anticlonal therapy in advanced cardiac AL amyloidosis. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as #NCT04131309.

papers.abstract: Abstract Red blood cells (RBCs) are transcriptionally silent yet dynamically remodel metabolism in response to oxygen tension. Using ultrapure human RBCs, we generated the deepest contamination-free proteome to date (3775 proteins) and mapped the oxygen-dependent interactome. These data sets revealed an oxygen-responsive metabolon centered on the Band 3 (SLC4A1) N terminus. We identified biliverdin reductase B (BLVRB) as a previously unrecognized Band 3 interactor that dissociates under hypoxia, coincident with increased Band 3–deoxyhemoglobin contacts. This reversible assembly functions as an oxygen-sensitive switch coordinating redox and glycolytic remodeling. Humanized mice lacking Band 3 N-terminal segments exhibited impaired oxygen-dependent regulation of BLVRB binding to Band 3, impaired hypoxic activation of glycolysis, reduced 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate synthesis, and diminished exercise tolerance, demonstrating physiological relevance. Population-scale cis–protein quantitative trait loci for SLC4A1 and BLVRB suggest functions beyond canonical heme catabolism. Mechanistically, in vitro biochemical analyses suggest that hemoglobin β, Band 3, and BLVRB can undergo S-nitrosation and may participate in transnitrosation reactions with the glycolytic enzyme glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, whose modification at C152 inhibits enzymatic activity in vitro. Collectively, these findings define a Band 3–BLVRB axis that integrates oxygen-dependent protein interactions with thiol-based redox chemistry, providing a framework for understanding how an anucleate cell achieves metabolic adaptability through reversible protein-protein interactions and posttranslational modification. These findings suggest that the perturbation of the Band 3–BLVRB axis may influence oxygen delivery and metabolic flexibility during hypoxic stress, with potential relevance to high-altitude adaptation, exercise physiology, and cardiopulmonary disease.

papers.abstract: Low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma (LGFMS) and sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma (SEF) represent a molecularly related spectrum of ultra-rare soft-tissue sarcomas characterised by recurrent FUS or EWSR1 rearrangements and frequent MUC4 expression. Despite sharing recurrent molecular alterations, their clinical behaviour differs markedly, positioning them at opposite ends of a biologically related spectrum with distinct clinical trajectories. This study aimed to characterise the clinicopathological features, molecular profiles, treatment approaches, and outcomes across this spectrum. We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients with LGFMS or SEF at a national EURACAN-designated sarcoma reference centre between 2013 and 2024. Clinicopathological characteristics, molecular findings, treatments, and outcomes were collected and analysed descriptively. Twenty patients were included: 11 (55%) LGFMS, six (30%) SEF and three (15%) hybrid tumours. MUC4 was positive in 13 cases (65%). Molecular analysis was informative in 19 patients (95%), with FUS or EWSR1 rearrangements in 16 (84%). FUS predominated (63%); EWSR1 rearrangements were confined to SEF (21%). Nineteen patients (95%) underwent curative-intent surgery. Local recurrence occurred in two (10%). Distant metastases developed in three (15%), all with SEF or hybrid histology. Metastatic progression was early (median 6 months), associated with high-risk histological features and EWSR1 rearrangement. SEF accounted for the only disease-related death; median overall survival was not reached, with 95% of patients alive at last follow-up. These findings highlight the divergent clinical behaviour across the LGFMS-SEF spectrum and support closer surveillance of high-risk tumours.

papers.abstract: In non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), EGFR and HER2 mutations are generally considered mutually exclusive events, with a co-occurrence probability estimated to be less than 1%. Patients with either EGFR or HER2 mutations tend to exhibit low PD-L1 expression levels. The simultaneous presence of both EGFR and HER2 mutations accompanied by high PD-L1 expression is exceedingly rare. This study reports a female patient who was admitted to the hospital after a routine physical examination revealed a right lung nodule and was diagnosed with "right lung adenocarcinoma (cT2aN2aM1c1, IVA; EGFR 21 L858R mutation; HER2 exon 8 mutation; PD-L1 TPS 60%)." The patient was immediately started on first-line third-generation EGFR-targeted therapy (Furmonertinib), but disease progression occurred after just 4.4 months (malignant pleural effusion and pericardial effusion). As the patient refused repeat biopsy, treatment with an ADC drug (Trastuzumab rezetecan) was initiated. Disease control was achieved after only one cycle of treatment, and the regimen was continued thereafter. The progression-free survival has exceeded 5.3 months, and at the time of writing this report, the disease remained well-controlled. This paper presents the first report of this rare and therapeutically challenging combination of molecular pathological features-concurrent EGFR and HER2 mutations with high PD-L1 expression in an NSCLC patient. When standard first-line third-generation EGFR-TKIs proved ineffective, the successful use of an anti-HER2 ADC drug to control the tumor demonstrates its potential clinical value. However, whether all patients initially presenting with this pathological molecular subtype will achieve consistent efficacy remains to be further investigated.

papers.abstract: Systemic inflammation is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of long-term health outcomes. The Inflammatory Burden Index (IBI), derived from C-reactive protein, neutrophil count, and lymphocyte count, integrates multiple components of systemic inflammatory and immune status. However, evidence regarding its association with long-term mortality among individuals with and without a history of cancer remains limited. We investigated the associations of IBI with mortality outcomes using two population-based cohorts, the UK Biobank (UKB) and the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES, 1999-2010), and an independent clinical cohort of patients with gastric cancer. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the associations between IBI and mortality outcomes. Stratified analyses were performed by history of cancer and among participants with digestive tract cancers, and sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess robustness. The UKB included 455,423 participants, of whom 54,813 had a history of cancer, and NHANES included 24,708 participants, of whom 2,159 had a history of cancer. Participants with a history of cancer were more frequently represented in the highest IBI quartile in both cohorts. Higher IBI was consistently associated with increased all-cause, cancer-specific, and CVD-specific mortality. In the UKB, among participants with a history of cancer, the highest versus lowest IBI quartile was associated with higher risks of all-cause (HR = 1.62, 95% CI: 1.53-1.71), cancer-specific (HR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.45-1.64), and CVD-specific mortality (HR = 1.81, 95% CI: 1.41-2.33). Consistent associations were observed in NHANES and remained robust in continuous and sensitivity analyses. Among participants with digestive tract cancers, higher IBI was associated with increased all-cause and cancer-specific mortality. In the independent gastric cancer cohort (n = 793), the highest IBI quartile was associated with poorer overall survival after multivariable adjustment (HR = 2.53, 95% CI: 1.59-4.02). Higher IBI was consistently associated with increased all-cause, cancer-specific, and CVD-specific mortality across population-based cohorts, with additional evidence from participants with digestive tract cancers and an independent gastric cancer cohort. These findings support the potential prognostic relevance of IBI as a readily accessible marker of systemic inflammatory burden.

papers.abstract: POLE-mutated endometrial carcinomas are associated with an excellent prognosis and have become an integral component of the molecular classification of endometrial carcinoma. However, the pathogenicity of many rare non-hotspot POLE exonuclease-domain variants remains uncertain, particularly when they occur in tumors harboring additional molecular alterations that may confound molecular classification. Histopathologic findings and immunohistochemical expression of mismatch repair proteins and p53 were evaluated. Targeted next-generation sequencing of tumor tissue was performed to characterize genomic alterations, microsatellite instability, tumor mutational burden, and the mutational spectrum. The non-hotspot POLE p.T278K variant was evaluated using the León-Castillo scoring framework. MLH1 promoter methylation was assessed by methylation-specific PCR to further characterize the subclonal MLH1/PMS2 loss. A 59-year-old woman with endometrioid endometrial carcinoma underwent total hysterectomy with surgical staging. Targeted next-generation sequencing identified a rare non-hotspot POLE exonuclease-domain variant, c.833C>A (p.T278K), together with two MSH6 frameshift variants, c.3261del (p.F1088Sfs*2) and c.3261dup (p.F1088Lfs*5). The tumor demonstrated an ultramutated genomic profile with a tumor mutational burden of 370.0 mutations/Mb and an MSI-H phenotype. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated subclonal loss of MLH1, PMS2, and MSH6 with retained MSH2 expression; MLH1 promoter methylation was also detected. This case adds clinicopathological and molecular evidence supporting the biological significance of the rare POLE p.T278K variant and illustrates a practical approach for interpreting uncommon POLE exonuclease-domain variants in endometrial carcinomas with multiple molecular classifiers. Accurate identification of the dominant molecular classifier is critical for appropriate molecular classification, prognostic assessment, and clinical management.

papers.abstract: PD-1 inhibitors are widely used anticancer drugs and frequently trigger immune-related adverse events, with thyroid dysfunction as the most prevalent. Suspected isolated central hypothyroidism emerging during PD-1 inhibitor therapy has rarely been documented. A 56-year-old man received pembrolizumab for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Before treatment, he had pre-existing Hashimoto's thyroiditis with low TT4 and normal TSH. He developed painless thyroiditis manifesting as transient thyrotoxicosis followed by primary hypothyroidism. Shortly after hypothyroidism was pharmacologically controlled, TSH progressively declined to the lower limit of detection, accompanied by low TT4. Pituitary MRI showed pituitary gland thinning without focal structural abnormalities. Integrating the clinical course, central hypothyroidism was considered. Given altered upper gastrointestinal anatomy after esophagectomy, split-dose levothyroxine was administered, and the patient's FT4 levels remained stable. This rare sequential evolution of thyroid dysfunction may represent an uncommon endocrine immune-related adverse event of immune checkpoint inhibitors.

papers.abstract: Health inequities in cancer care persist, indicating that advancing equity requires not only understanding inequities but also transforming how cancer research is developed and conducted. Although equity-oriented and community-engaged approaches have advanced important principles for research, there is limited understanding of the conditions and processes required to translate these principles into practice within cancer care systems, including how research agendas can be collaboratively developed to reflect community and health system needs. This Perspective describes the co-design and implementation of a provincial Health Equity Workshop in Alberta, Canada, as a practice-based example of how a cancer care system operationalized Patient-Oriented Research principles to support equity-oriented research agenda development. Guided by Patient-Oriented Research and informed by the Health Equity Implementation Framework, the initiative involved a twelve-member working group comprising people with lived experience of cancer, representatives of community organizations, health system leaders, and researchers who co-designed and facilitated a two-day workshop involving 43 participants. Reflections from the initiative highlighted relational, organizational, and practical conditions that shaped equity-oriented engagement, including trust-building, shared leadership, compensation and resource supports, institutional commitment, and attention to system-level barriers affecting participation. The workshop demonstrated how co-design can embed equity from the earliest stages of research agenda development by bringing together diverse forms of expertise to shape what research is needed and how it should be conducted. This Perspective offers practical insights for researchers, health systems, and community partners seeking to advance equitable cancer research and care.

papers.abstract: Alveolar soft part sarcoma (ASPS) is a rare type of soft tissue sarcoma; ASPS originating in the central nervous system is even rarer. Previous literature has generally described it as having an indolent course with a favorable prognosis following surgical resection. This report presents a case of a 31-year-old woman with primary intracranial alveolar soft part sarcoma (PIASPS) that exhibited the opposite characteristics, demonstrating high invasiveness. The patient underwent gross total resection during the initial surgery, and postoperative histopathological examination and immunohistochemistry confirmed the diagnosis of PIASPS. Rapid local recurrence occurred just over two months after surgery; the tumor exhibited abnormally high proliferative activity, with an initial Ki-67 index of approximately 65%, which rose to 75% following recurrence. Molecular testing also revealed a complex mutation profile, including a BRAF p.V600E mutation, a TP53 p.D281E missense mutation, a TERT promoter mutation, an NBN truncating mutation, an HGF nonsense mutation, and an RPSAP52-HMGA2 fusion; these molecular events may have contributed to the rapid tumor recurrence, although their individual and combined effects require further functional validation. Following recurrence, the patient underwent a second surgery, followed by adjuvant radiotherapy and concurrent oral anlotinib; however, the patient died two months following the completion of radiotherapy, with an overall survival of eight months. Characterized by rapid early postoperative recurrence, sustained high proliferative activity, and complex molecular features, this case challenges the traditional perception of PIASPS as an indolent tumor. This case suggests that a high Ki-67 index combined with molecular subtyping may help identify potentially aggressive subtypes; its value in guiding decisions regarding adjuvant therapy may be further explored in future studies.

papers.abstract: Gastric cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, largely due to invasion, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. Dysregulated cholesterol metabolism is increasingly recognised as a driver of gastric cancer progression, but how intracellular cholesterol trafficking contributes to malignant junctional remodelling remains poorly understood. MLN64/STARD3 is a cholesterol-binding lipid transfer protein associated with cancer progression, yet its functional role in gastric cancer cell architecture and aggressiveness has not been fully defined. In this study, we investigated whether MLN64 is associated with cholesterol-dependent tight junction organisation and malignant behaviour in gastric cancer cells. Stable MLN64 knockdown in AGS and HGC-27 cells reduced membrane-associated free cholesterol, as shown by an approximately 50% decrease in the Filipin III membrane/cytoplasm fluorescence ratio in both cell lines. MLN64 depletion was also associated with reduced ZO-1 protein abundance, disrupted junctional ZO-1 localisation, and impaired tight junction integrity, including reduced transepithelial resistance, altered impedance, and increased paracellular permeability. Functionally, MLN64 depletion attenuated gastric cancer cell proliferation and invasive capacity, supporting an association between this cholesterol-trafficking axis, junctional organisation, and aggressive cellular phenotypes. To explore the pharmacological tractability of this pathway, in silico screening of an FDA-approved drug library identified Digoxin and Targretin as candidate compounds predicted to interact with the MLN64 START domain. Digoxin showed a favourable predicted binding energy of -13.73 kcal/mol. Functional validation showed that these agents phenocopied several effects of MLN64 depletion, including altered cholesterol distribution, reduced junctional ZO-1 organisation, impaired adhesion/migration dynamics, and reduced barrier function. Together, these findings identify MLN64 as a regulator associated with cholesterol-dependent tight junction remodelling in gastric cancer cells. Digoxin and Targretin provide preliminary evidence that this pathway may be pharmacologically tractable; however, direct target-engagement and rescue studies will be required to establish causality and determine whether their effects are mediated through direct interaction with MLN64. The MLN64- cholesterol axis may represent a potential vulnerability in gastric cancer membrane organisation and progression.

papers.abstract: To improve the diagnostic accuracy of benign versus malignant parotid tumors using non-contrast CT. We propose a clinician-in-the-loop hybrid framework that mitigates low soft-tissue contrast by fusing semi-automated 3D visual features with expert semantic descriptors. This multi-center retrospective study analyzed non-contrast CTs from 367 patients. We developed AttenNet, a semi-automated model. First, an nnU-Net module automates 3D tumor segmentation, eliminating manual bounding boxes. A 3D-ResNet backbone then extracts volumetric features, which are dynamically fused with radiologist-provided semantic labels via a Multi-Head Cross-Attention Fusion (MHAF) mechanism. This allows the network to query visual morphology based on expert priors. Diagnostic performance and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) interpretability were evaluated. The segmentation achieved a median Dice of 0.827. AttenNet (3D-ResNet) yielded an AUC of 0.908, significantly outperforming the image-only 3D-ResNet (AUC: 0.741) and expert-feature models (AUC: 0.821). External validation (n = 20) reached an AUC of 0.560-0.910.However, given the extremely small sample size, these results must be interpreted strictly as an exploratory proof-of-concept rather than definitive confirmation of generalizability. Grad-CAM confirmed that AttenNet highlights clinically essential geometric indicators-specifically tumor margins and internal heterogeneity-for differentiating malignancy, whereas single-modality baselines focused on background artifacts. This clinician-in-the-loop paradigm successfully integrates spatial imaging with expert reasoning. While multimodal fusion drove the primary performance gains, the MHAF mechanism provided enhanced spatial interpretability.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to relieve radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) by assessing the use of prophylactic pirfenidone. Subjects were lung cancer patients with prior ICI treatment who received thoracic radiotherapy. Patients with lung cancer were enrolled in this phase II single-arm study. All candidates had a history of prior ICI exposure (≥2 cycles; interval ≤6 months) scheduled for thoracic radiotherapy (≥50 Gy). Patients received oral pirfenidone (1800 mg/day) from one week pre-radiotherapy to four weeks post-completion. The primary endpoint was the 6-month incidence of ≥grade 2 RILI, compared to a 40% historical control (p0=0.40; p1=0.22; α=0.10; power=80%). Secondary endpoints included pulmonary function (DLCO%, FVC%) and safety. A total of 39 patients were enrolled in this trial. At the 6-month follow-up, the incidence of grade 2 or higher RILI was 23.1% (9/39; 95% CI: 11.1%-39.3%). This rate was statistically significantly lower than the 40% incidence from the historical control cohort (p=0.0205). Grade 3 RILI occurred in 7.7% (3/39); no grade 4-5 events occurred. Mean DLCO% declined by 7.6 ± 5.4% at 3 months and 6.5 ± 5.8% at 6 months. The pirfenidone completion rate was 84.6% (median relative dose intensity: 89.3%). Common adverse events were fatigue (43.6%), nausea (41.0%), and appetite loss (33.3%), mostly grade 1-2. Preventive use of pirfenidone was associated with a lower observed incidence and severity of RILI than the predefined historical control in ICI-pretreated lung cancer patients receiving thoracic radiotherapy. Additionally, the intervention showed a potential protective trend for pulmonary diffusion function. These findings require further validation in a phase III trial.

papers.abstract: Abstract Leukemia stem cells (LSCs) drive acute myeloid leukemia (AML) initiation, relapse, and chemoresistance, yet the core posttranslational events sustaining LSC maintenance remain poorly defined. Here, through phosphoproteomic profiling of normal hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) vs LSC-enriched populations, we identified DEK phosphorylation as a critical modification during leukemogenesis. Functional studies in MLL-AF9– and HOXA9/MEIS1-driven AML mouse models, as well as patient-derived xenografts, demonstrate that DEK deficiency impairs LSC maintenance and AML progression. Moreover, DEK deletion enhances LSC chemosensitivity to the standard-of-care combination of azacitidine and venetoclax, whereas DEK overexpression confers robust chemoresistance. Mechanistically, DEK recruits the transcription factor GA repeat binding protein α (GABPA) to upregulate the transcriptional cofactor PBX3, a key oncogenic driver in AML, thereby sustaining the leukemogenic transcriptional program. This DEK-GABPA interaction strictly depends on DEK phosphorylation at Ser301/303/306/307 (the 4S sites), which stabilizes the conformation of the DEK-GABPA complex. We identify casein kinase 2 (CK2) as the upstream kinase that directly phosphorylates DEK-4S sites. Importantly, blockade of DEK phosphorylation via 4S site mutagenesis or treatment with the clinical-stage CK2 inhibitor CX-4945 selectively depletes LSCs while sparing normal HSPCs. Furthermore, combining CX-4945 with venetoclax promotes LSC apoptosis and represses the PBX3-driven leukemogenic transcriptional program, exhibiting synergistic anti-AML effects both in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, our findings uncover a previously unrecognized phosphorylation event (DEK-4S phosphorylation) that sustains LSCs and establish the CK2-DEK axis as a promising LSC-specific therapeutic strategy for AML.

papers.abstract: Abstract Primary cutaneous T-cell lymphomas (CTCL) are a heterogeneous group of extranodal non-Hodgkin lymphomas. Outcomes for patients with advanced-stage disease are suboptimal, because few complete and durable responses are achieved with currently available therapeutic agents. However, improved understanding of oncogenic transcriptional programs in malignant T cells and their engagement with the tumor microenvironment (TME) may unveil therapeutic vulnerabilities. Therefore, we have compiled the largest available single-cell RNA-sequencing CTCL atlas that includes >2 million skin and blood cells from 116 individual patients. We identified recurrent transcriptional programs in malignant T cells, a subset of which are associated with GATA binding protein 3–dependent transcriptional programs, especially in the setting of large cell transformation and advanced-stage disease. Many of the transcriptional programs identified are therapeutically targetable with clinically available agents, including HDAC, XPO1, CDK9, JAK/CSF1R, and IKZF1/IKZF3 antagonists. The CTCL TME is dominated by infiltrating and exhausted effector and cytotoxic T cells that are restrained by a robust infiltrate of regulatory T cells, transcriptionally polarized monocytes/macrophages, and cancer-associated fibroblasts. Collectively, these findings have significant implications for the rational design of combinatorial strategies targeting immune checkpoints, including programmed cell death protein 1. We have identified transcriptional programs, driven by oncogenic transcription factors, and constituents of the TME as therapeutic vulnerabilities in CTCL, and hope that the CTCL atlas constructed will provide a valuable resource for future studies exploiting these therapeutic vulnerabilities.

papers.abstract: Epigenetic silencing of tumour suppressor genes is a pivotal early event in colorectal cancer (CRC) pathogenesis. PDZ and LIM Domain 4 (PDLIM4) is a member of the PDZ-LIM family with context-dependent roles in tumour progression across different malignancies. However, its specific role and epigenetic regulation in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain elusive. We integrated multi-omics datasets and clinical cohorts to evaluate PDLIM4 expression and promoter methylation. Stool DNA was analyzed to assess the feasibility of non-invasive detection of PDLIM4 promoter methylation. PDLIM4 knockout and overexpression cell lines were constructed to perform functional assays including proliferation, apoptosis, and stemness. In vivo experiments were validated utilizing xenograft mice or an azoxymethane (AOM)/ dextran sulphate sodium salt (DSS) CRC mouse model with intestinal epithelial cell-specific overexpression of PDLIM4. Mechanistic investigations were conducted using coimmunoprecipitation coupled with mass spectrometry, RNA sequencing, ChIP-qPCR and pharmacological rescue experiments. We identified a progressive loss of PDLIM4 protein along the normal-adenoma-carcinoma sequence, driven by DNMT3A-mediated promoter hypermethylation, and lower PDLIM4 expression was associated with adverse patient prognosis. PDLIM4 methylation was also significantly increased in stool DNA from CRC patients compared with healthy controls. Mechanistically, genetic ablation of PDLIM4 significantly blunted the therapeutic efficacy of the DNA demethylating agent 5-Azacytidine against CRC. Functionally, PDLIM4 restoration suppressed CRC cell proliferation and stemness while enhancing apoptosis in vitro, and reduced tumour growth in both AOM/DSS and xenograft models in vivo. At the molecular level, PDLIM4 interacted with BTF3 and promoted its autophagic-lysosomal degradation, thereby limiting PI3K/Akt signalling, with NTRK2 identified as a potential transcriptional target linking BTF3 to PI3K/Akt activation. DNMT3A-mediated silencing of PDLIM4 is an early epigenetic event that facilitates CRC progression. PDLIM4 suppresses tumour growth by promoting BTF3 degradation, thereby restricting PI3K/Akt signalling. Thus, PDLIM4 methylation may have potential as a biomarker for early CRC detection. DNMT3A-mediated PDLIM4 promoter hypermethylation is an early event in colorectal tumorigenesis. Restoring PDLIM4 suppresses CRC proliferation and stemness while promoting apoptosis in vitro and in vivo. PDLIM4 promotes the autophagic-lysosomal degradation of BTF3 and restrains PI3K/Akt signalling. Stool DNA analysis supports the potential of PDLIM4 methylation as a non-invasive CRC biomarker.

papers.abstract: Imaging-guided interventional radiotherapy (IG-IRT) is the standard of care for locally advanced cervical cancer but remains time-consuming and operator-dependent. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to improve efficiency and reproducibility. A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searching PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between 2010 and 2026 investigating AI-based imaging applications in cervical IRT. Eligible studies included original research evaluating segmentation (targets and organ at risk), planning, reconstruction, image registration and applicator selection. Fifty-two studies were included. Deep learning-based segmentation showed variable performance across anatomical structures and studies, with Dice coefficients approaching or exceeding 0.90 for some organs at risk and target volumes in the best-performing models. Individual studies reported shorter processing times, reduced contouring variability, accurate applicator reconstruction, and potential support for applicator selection. However, the substantial methodological and clinical heterogeneity precluded direct comparisons among AI approaches. The available studies suggest that AI may support the automation of selected workflow steps and assist treatment-related decision-making in image-guided cervical interventional radiotherapy. While several applications have achieved high technical performance, most remain at the proof-of-concept stage, and robust external validation and prospective clinical evaluation are needed before routine clinical adoption.

papers.abstract: Gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis (GCPM), particularly associated with diffuse and poorly cohesive cancers, in which tumour cells grow singly or in small, loosely associated groups, presents an anatomical and immunological treatment challenge. This review examines the peritoneal surface and surrounding fluid as an interacting immune compartment comprising tumour implants, malignant ascites, free tumour cells, stroma and immune populations. Human studies identify cytotoxic-cell depletion or exhaustion, macrophage-rich ascites and suppressive soluble mediators; experimental findings support complement-pathway involvement in immune-checkpoint ligand expression. These observations offer a biological explanation for impaired local immunity but do not establish clinical resistance to checkpoint inhibition. Systemic therapy remains the treatment backbone, yet pivotal trials rarely report the Peritoneal Cancer Index (PCI), cytology, ascites response or peritoneal-specific progression. Early studies combine checkpoint blockade with pressurised intraperitoneal aerosol chemotherapy (PIPAC), repeated intraperitoneal paclitaxel or hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC); direct intraperitoneal antibodies, cytokines and cellular therapies are also under investigation. Feasibility and local pharmacodynamic changes do not establish synergistic benefit. Future trials should compare an added intraperitoneal treatment against an otherwise identical systemic regimen, collect matched blood, ascites and peritoneal tissue samples over time, and relate immune changes to cytological clearance, PCI, symptoms and survival. Operative consolidation requires a separate randomised assessment in prospectively defined responders. Treatment continuity, quality of life, nutrition and hospital-free survival are essential measures of net benefit.

papers.abstract: Abstract Socioeconomic status (SES) is well recognized as an important determinant of cancer incidence and survival. However, its impact on outcomes in patients with mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) remains poorly characterized. We conducted a nationwide, population-based retrospective longitudinal study using German cancer registry data, including all patients diagnosed with MCL between 2013 and 2023. Regional SES was assessed annually at the district level using quintiles of the German Index of Socioeconomic Deprivation. The primary outcomes were 5-year absolute survival (AS) and relative survival (RS) as a proxy for disease-specific survival. A total of 8871 patients were included. Five-year AS and RS were 62.6% (95% CI, 61.5–63.7) and 72.1% (95% CI, 70.8–73.4), respectively. However, no meaningful differences in AS were observed between patients residing in districts of the lowest and highest SES quintiles (62.0% vs 63.1%). This nationwide population-based study indicates that regional socioeconomic deprivation was not associated with clinically relevant differences in survival outcomes among MCL patients in Germany between 2013 and 2023. These findings differ from previously described patterns in other lymphomas, suggesting that biological disease characteristics may exert a stronger influence on MCL survival than social determinants.

papers.abstract: Abstract Dysbiosis after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (allo-HSCT) predisposes to acute gastrointestinal (GI) graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) are prebiotics that establish a favorable intestinal microbiome. We hypothesized that peritransplant HMOs would reduce dysbiosis, and conducted a prospective phase 1/2 study in which 70 patients received oral, daily 2’-fucosyllactose (2’-FL), the most abundant HMO, from start of conditioning through day +30. Primary phase 1 and phase 2 end points were safety and tolerability of 2′-FL and longitudinal preservation of microbiome diversity, respectively. Phase 1 and phase 2 patients with ≥60% adherence were evaluated by correlative analyses. Twenty-nine age-matched patients with available samples in our institutional biorepository served as contemporary controls. 2′-FL was safe and well tolerated on the phase 1 study, which established dosing for the phase 2 study. Shannon diversity was preserved in 2′-FL recipients and declined from baseline to day +30 in controls (P = .04). Generalized linear mixed model analysis revealed higher association of Bifidobacteria and Blautia with 2′-FL (adjusted P< .05). Higher fecal isoleucine (P = .005), tyrosine (P = .05), and taurine (P = .04) were observed in 2′-FL recipients, all associated with protection and regeneration of intestinal epithelium. Lower plasma regulatory islet-derived 3α (P = .053) and suppressor of tumorigenicity 2 levels (P = .038) were observed in 2′-FL recipients compared with controls. Incidence of grade II-IV acute GI GVHD was 0% in 2′-FL recipients compared with 17% in controls (P = .009). Adenovirus reactivation was 0% in 2′-FL recipients compared with 17% in controls (P = .009). 2′-FL is safe and modifies the gut microbiome in children after allo-HSCT. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as #NCT04263597.

papers.abstract: Abstract Direct targeting of the oncoprotein MYC has not yet been successful. Here we report a novel dual protein degrader, GT19630, which binds directly to MYC and G1 to S phase transition protein 1 (GSPT1). GT19630 disrupts a novel feedforward loop of MYC and GSPT1, in which MYC promotes transcription of GSPT1, and GSPT1 senses the stop codon of MYC to properly terminate its translation. The agent induces an integrated stress response and abrogates oxidative phosphorylation through inhibition of the tricarboxylic acid cycle, resulting in apoptosis. GT19630 has superior activity compared with GSPT1-targeting molecular glues. GT19630 induces profound antiproliferative effects and apoptosis at low nanomolar concentrations in a multitude of leukemia and lymphoma cell lines and primary samples, including those with TP53 mutations. GT19630 is highly active in vivo in models of therapy-resistant hematologic malignancies, including Burkitt lymphoma, acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and multiple myeloma. CD34+ AML blasts overexpress MYC protein compared with normal hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs), and GT19630 induces greater cytotoxicity in AML cells compared with normal HSPCs. Further, GT19630 restores sensitivity to venetoclax and profoundly prolongs survival in vivo in venetoclax-resistant AML. GT19630 was well tolerated in humanized Crbn mice. In conclusion, our data support the development of the MYC/GSPT1 degrader GT19630 as a therapeutic strategy for MYC-driven hematologic malignancies.

papers.abstract: Abstract Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) is an orphan, aggressive hematologic malignancy characterized by high CD123 expression. Tagraxofusp (TAG), a CD123-directed toxin, is the first approved therapy. Prior studies demonstrated BPDCN dependence on BCL2, sensitivity to venetoclax (VEN), and reversal of TAG resistance with azacitidine (AZA). We conducted a phase 2 study evaluating combination therapy with TAG, AZA, and VEN in patients with BPDCN. Patients with previously untreated (1L) or relapsed/refractory (R/R) BPDCN received 28-day cycles of AZA (75 mg/m2 on days 1-7), VEN (400 mg on days 1-21), and TAG (12 μg/kg on days 4-6). Eligibility followed TAG guidelines to mitigate risk of capillary leak syndrome (CLS). Twenty-seven patients were enrolled (16 1L, 11 R/R), with median age of 70 years (range, 21-81). Composite complete remission (composed of: complete remission [CR], CR with incomplete count recovery, and CR clinical) rates were 88% in 1L and 64% in R/R cohorts. Median duration of response was not reached in 1L and was 7.2 months in R/R patients. CLS occurred in 15% of patients, most were grade 2. In the 1L cohort, median overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were not reached; the 2-year OS was 65% and 2-year PFS was 53%. Median OS in R/R patients was 8.4 months. A high proportion of patients proceeded to allogeneic stem cell transplantation in remission (63% in 1L, including 10/11 patients aged ≤75 years; 55% in R/R). TAG-AZA-VEN is highly active in both 1L and relapsed BPDCN with a predictable and manageable safety profile, supporting its use as a new therapeutic option. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as #NCT03113643.

papers.abstract: Conventional MRI may not fully reflect the biological activity of vorasidenib. PET may detect treatment-related metabolic changes before structural changes become evident on MRI. We evaluated longitudinal PET and MRI changes in patients with IDH-mutant gliomas receiving vorasidenib. VORAFET is a longitudinal study of adults with IDH-mutant gliomas treated with vorasidenib. Eligible patients had predominantly non-enhancing WHO grade 2 or 3 gliomas, had not received prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was longitudinal metabolic and structural imaging response according to PET RANO 1.0 and RANO 2.0. Integrated [¹⁸F]FET PET/MRI was performed at baseline and every 3 months. Thirty-nine patients were included; at baseline, 23 and 29 had PET and MRI-measurable disease. As best response, PET RANO 1.0 identified 2 complete and 12 partial responses, yielding an ORR of 60.9%; median time to first response was 4.5 months (range 3-12 months). RANO 2.0 showed no complete or partial responses, whereas 5 patients achieved minor response at a median of 9 months (range 6-12 months). Progressive disease occurred in 6 of 39 patients (15.4%) according to PET RANO 1.0 and in 1 of 39 (2.6%) according to RANO 2.0. Patients with PET-PD more often had subtle contrast enhancement and showed higher baseline FLAIR volume, MTV, TBRmax, and TBRmean. PET RANO 1.0 identified metabolic changes during vorasidenib treatment that were not always reflected by RANO 2.0 assessment. Longer follow-up is needed to clarify the relationship between PET metabolic changes and MRI findings and to determine their clinical significance.

papers.abstract: Adoptive T-cell therapies require T cells to sustain cytotoxic function for as long as tumor persists. In this issue, two independent studies converge on a ubiquitin-dependent pathway, centered on the cullin-5 (CUL5)-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase (CRL5) complex, as an intrinsic brake on T-cell function under repetitive antigen stimulation. Genetic disruption of individual CRL5 components preserves cytotoxicity during repeated tumor challenge. Saco and colleagues demonstrate similar benefits with pharmacologic inhibition of CRL5 and related ubiquitin ligase complexes, whereas Bachl and colleagues extend the genetic benefit across multiple antigens and receptor architectures. Targeting this pathway offers a strategy to improve T-cell functional persistence and therapeutic durability. See related article by Bachl et al., p. XXX . See related article by Saco et al., p. papers.abstract: Abstract Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by antibody-mediated platelet destruction and impaired regulatory T-cell (Treg) function, yet its molecular basis remains poorly defined. Here, we show that CD4+ naive T cells from patients with ITP exhibit diminished T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling and impaired in vitro Treg induction relative to healthy controls. RNA sequencing revealed widespread dysregulation of alternative splicing, most notably exon 8 skipping in LCK, a kinase central to TCR signaling and Treg differentiation. Using an LCK minigene combined with RNA pull-down mass spectrometry and RNA immunoprecipitation assays, we identified the splicing factor SRSF1 as a direct upstream regulator of LCK exon 8 skipping. Notably, SRSF1 expression was reduced in CD4+ naive T cells from patients with ITP, and its overexpression restored in vitro Treg induction capacity. Antisense oligonucleotide–mediated blockade of SRSF1 binding to LCK enhanced exon 8 skipping and attenuated TCR activation in Jurkat cells. Although murine Lck lacks the human-specific recursive splicing sites required for exon 8 exclusion, the adoptive transfer of CD4+ naive T cells expressing the exon 8–skipped murine Lck into CD61-knockout mice significantly reduced Treg proportions and platelet counts in an active ITP model. Mechanistically, Jurkat cells engineered to express only the exon 8–skipped LCK variant showed markedly reduced binding to ZAP70 and CD3ζ, which may partly account for the attenuated TCR signaling and downstream FOXP3 induction. Together, these findings define a novel SRSF1-LCK splicing axis that may regulate Treg development in ITP.

papers.abstract: Abstract Immunotherapy has revolutionized the treatment of solid cancers in recent years. However, T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas (T-NHL) originate from immune cells themselves and are biologically heterogeneous, rendering investigations of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) mechanisms of action complex. Although case reports and individual anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL) patients enrolled in T-NHL trials demonstrated favorable responses to ICIs, hyperprogression was observed in other T-NHL subtypes. We therefore used a syngeneic mouse model of anaplastic lymphoma kinase positive (ALK+) ALCL to investigate immune surveillance and ICI-induced immune response. Transplantation experiments combined with the depletion of relevant immune axes revealed that ALCL immune surveillance is mediated by CD4+ T cells and natural killer cells. Innate and adaptive immune cell infiltration was confirmed in a large series of primary human ALK+ ALCL samples. ICI monotherapy demonstrated robust efficacy in murine ALCL, inducing complete remissions in ∼50% of treated animals. Mechanistically, PD-L1 blockade reversed regulatory T cell-mediated immunosuppression and increased the frequency of circulating effector CD8+ T lymphocytes, thereby significantly prolonging survival. Importantly, CD4+ T cells proved indispensable for driving and sustaining immunotherapy-induced antitumor responses in murine ALCL. CD4+ T cells of nonresponder animals exhibited an exhausted phenotype and a transcriptomic T helper 22–like signature, implicating persistent T-cell exhaustion and polarization as a meaningful immune evasion mechanism. Our findings uncover CD4+ T cells as key players in spontaneous and immunotherapy-mediated anti–T-cell lymphoma immunity, which demonstrates the critically needed preclinical proof-of-concept for the safe and effective use of immunotherapy for ALCL.

papers.abstract: Abstract Patients with acute leukemias harboring translocations involving gene lysine methyltransferase 2A (KMT2A) have a poor prognosis due to chemotherapy resistance with rapid relapse following standard treatments. The resulting KMT2A fusion proteins dysregulate gene expression, leading to an upregulation of leukemogenic transcription factors such as HOXA9 and MEIS1, which drives leukemic transformation. Although menin inhibitors are proving to be promising new therapeutics for patients with KMT2A-rearranged (KMT2Ar) acute leukemia, resistance mechanisms have already been described and new therapeutic approaches for this patient subgroup must be identified. Here, a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen in a KMT2Ar B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia cell line identified the deubiquitinase ubiquitin-specific peptidase 22 (USP22) as a novel regulator of MEIS1 protein stability. USP22 is a member of the Spt-Ada-Gcn5 acetyltransferase multiprotein complex, which has crucial functions in shaping the chromatin landscape and modulating transcription. Genetic depletion of USP22 impaired cellular growth and proliferation in KMT2Ar acute leukemia models. Chromatin immunoprecipitation revealed cooperative binding between USP22 and MEIS1 at critical oncogenic target genes, suggesting that USP22 safeguards leukemogenic transcription by protecting MEIS1 from proteasomal degradation. Genetic or chemical inhibition of USP22 led to the polyubiquitination of MEIS1, resulting in proteasomal degradation and downregulation of the expression of target genes. Our study identifies USP22 as a novel regulator of MEIS1 protein stability that could potentially be exploited as a therapeutic target in the future in KMT2Ar leukemias.

papers.abstract: Postoperative stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT) is the standard adjuvant treatment after resection of brain metastases. It nevertheless requires delineation of a dynamic postsurgical cavity, delays local treatment by 3 to 6 weeks (and thus resumption of systemic therapy) and carries substantial risks of radiation necrosis and leptomeningeal disease. Preoperative SRT targets an intact lesion and may address some of these limitations. In this open-label, single-arm, multicenter phase 2 trial, eligible adults had a Karnofsky performance status ≥70 and up to four brain metastases, including one resectable lesion ≤5 cm, from breast, non-small cell lung, kidney, or digestive cancer or melanoma. Patients received preoperative SRT (three fractions of 7.7 Gy prescribed to the encompassing 70% isodose line, equivalent to 11Gy per fraction at the isocenter) followed by surgical resection within 3 days of the last fraction. The primary outcome was 6-month local control on centrally reviewed MRI. Secondary outcomes included index-lesion radiation necrosis, leptomeningeal disease, distant intracranial control, overall survival, toxicity, cognition, and quality of life. Of 73 patients assessed, 67 were eligible and 63 received both SRT and surgery. Median age was 62 years. At a median follow-up of 12.7 months, the 6-month local control rate was 100% (95% CI, 95%-100%), meeting the primary endpoint; the 12-month rate was 96.4% (95% CI, 87%-99%). No leptomeningeal disease occurred. The 1-year cumulative incidence of index-lesion radiation necrosis was 7% (95% CI, 2%-16%), meeting the key secondary endpoint. Distant intracranial failure occurred in 22 patients (35%); 12-month overall survival was 81.2% (95% CI, 70%-89%). Postoperative complications occurred in 4 patients (6.3%); cognition and quality of life remained stable over the 12 months of protocol follow-up. Three-fraction preoperative SRT followed by resection was associated with high local control, low radiation necrosis, and no leptomeningeal disease, supporting evaluation in ongoing randomized trials.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is an endocrine and metabolic disorder associated with adverse perinatal and long-term health outcomes, yet its impact on cancer risk in children remains unclear. Methods We conducted a nationwide, register-based matched cohort study in Sweden, including children of primiparous women with (N = 22 955) and without PMOS (N = 103 613) born between 1973 and 2018. Children were followed from birth until cancer diagnosis, death, or December 2018. Conditional Cox proportional hazards models estimated the adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) with 95% CI, incorporating time-varying effects when the proportional hazards assumption was violated. Results During follow-up, 666 children were diagnosed with cancer. Compared with children born to women without PMOS, overall cancer risk among children of women with PMOS differed by sex and over time. Among sons, higher hazards at 1 year were observed (aHR = 4.17; 95% CI = 2.51 to 6.93), decreasing by 10 years (aHR = 1.53; 95% CI = 1.08 to 2.18). In daughters, hazard ratios did not indicate a change in overall cancer risk compared to reference. When both sexes were combined, risk of lymphatic and hematopoietic malignancies was higher (aHR = 2.43; 95% CI = 1.36 to 4.33). Competing risks of death did not materially alter the associations. Conclusions Overall cancer risk among children born to women with PMOS differed by sex and over time, with higher risks in sons during early life. These findings suggest that maternal PMOS may be associated with differential cancer susceptibility across the life course.

papers.abstract: Abstract Residential environmental chemical exposures have been associated with elevated cancer risks. This study examined the risk associated with living near Superfund sites for leukemia and lymphoma—two “indicator” cancers with high sensitivity to environmental chemical exposures. Analyzing 127 locations with available data (55 New York City neighborhoods and 72 counties, totaling 39.25% of the US population; 23 with large Superfund sites), the study found modestly higher area-level incidence rates of leukemia and lymphoma in locations classified as affected by Superfund sites. For lymphoma, estimated incidence rate ratio was 1.07 (95% CI = 1.02 to 1.11) among individuals aged 20-49 years and 1.05 (95% CI = 1.02 to 1.09) among individuals aged 50-64 years, corresponding to a 1.19 and 1.14 area-level relative risk respectively for the two groups living within 2 km (New York City) or 5 km (elsewhere) of a Superfund site. As many Superfund sites are located around population centers, these findings highlight the need for mitigating such exposures and cancer risks.

papers.abstract: Abstract Characterizing the genealogy of tumor cells and their population dynamics is central to our understanding of the evolution of cancer. While direct monitoring of the tumor evolutionary process is impractical, we leverage advances in phylogenetics and phylodynamics to explore the evolutionary dynamics of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) using single-cell whole exome sequencing data from 351 tumor cells across 11 NSCLC patients, predominantly focusing on the primary tumors and early stages of NSCLC. Our results reveal distinct phylogenetic tree shapes and evolutionary trajectories across different stages of NSCLC evolution. However, this intricate and multi-phase evolutionary process cannot be fully elucidated by current tumor models. Herein, we hypothesize that tumors progress through the following phases: (1) an initial rapid expansion through Big Bang-like growth, (2) a prolonged plateau period of non-progression with possible accumulation of neutral substitutions, (3) a subsequent phase where adaptive substitutions accumulate gradually, (4) a bottleneck event where selectively advantageous subclones acquire invasive capabilities (characterized by a pattern of punctuated evolution), and, potentially, a rapid expansion leading to metastasis. This work highlights the use of single-cell phylogenetics and phylodynamics for interpreting the evolution of NSCLC, with potential in predicting cancer progression, resistance mechanisms, and treatment response.

papers.abstract: Background: Prehabilitation is recommended to reduce surgery-related functional decline but is not routinely integrated into presurgical breast cancer care, often resulting in rehabilitation being delayed until after surgery. We conducted a retrospective comparative effectiveness study evaluating outcomes associated with real-world prehabilitation versus delayed rehabilitation care models. Methods: Women who began rehabilitation before (prehabilitation; n=416) or after breast cancer surgery (delayed rehabilitation; n=232) were identified from the electronic medical record. Upper extremity function and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) outcomes were extracted presurgery, postsurgery, and at final evaluation. Adjusted linear mixed-effect models examined change over time and between-group differences, and logistic regression estimated likelihood of achieving normal limits. Analyses were conducted overall and stratified by surgery type. Rehabilitation utilization and recovery to baseline levels among patients who received prehabilitation were summarized descriptively. Results: Prehabilitation was associated with superior postsurgery function and HRQoL, as well as higher odds of achieving normal limits, compared with delayed rehabilitation. Both groups improved during postoperative rehabilitation; however, functional outcomes and strength remained superior among patients who received prehabilitation at final evaluation. Benefits of prehabilitation were most pronounced among women undergoing mastectomy or bilateral mastectomy, although meaningful benefits were also observed following lumpectomy. All patients who received prehabilitation recovered to baseline levels on at least one outcome. Across the perioperative period, patients who received prehabilitation attended fewer visits than those who received delayed rehabilitation (median, 5 vs 7; P =.008). Conclusions: Both prehabilitation and delayed rehabilitation supported recovery of upper extremity functioning and HRQoL following breast cancer surgery. However, prehabilitation may represent a more effective and efficient care model—particularly for women undergoing more extensive surgical procedures—achieving comparable or better outcomes with fewer visits. These findings support integration of prehabilitation into breast cancer surgical care pathways.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Survivors of childhood cancer (CCS) have higher risk of developing ischaemic heart disease (IHD), however, data on coronary anatomy, revascularisations, and prognosis remain limited. The objective was to investigate angiographic findings, invasive treatment patterns and mortality in CCS with IHD compared with controls without a history of childhood cancer. Methods This was a nationwide retrospective cohort-study of all 5-year survivors of leukaemia, lymphoma, or central nervous system cancer who subsequently developed IHD, with index cancer between 1958-2021. CCS were compared with population-based controls with IHD matched on cancer date by age, sex and residence. Results 136 CCS and 667 controls with IHD were included. CCS were a median of 5.2 years younger than controls at diagnosis of IHD. CCS had a higher prevalence of left main coronary artery (LMCA) stenosis (25.0% vs. 6.5%; p < 0.001) and multivessel disease (51.2% vs. 39.4%; p = 0.043). Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) was more frequently performed in CCS (22.8% vs. 11.4%; p < 0.001), although after adjusting for relevant covariates the difference was attenuated. After a median follow-up of 5.4 years following IHD diagnosis, CCS had higher hazard of all-cause mortality (HR 1.83, 95% CI 1.31-2.54; p < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 2.04; 95% CI 1.42-2.95; p < 0.001). Conclusions CCS who developed IHD demonstrate a higher burden of extensive coronary artery disease, characterized by increased prevalence of LMCA stenosis and multivessel disease. Although overall revascularisation rates were similar, CCS experienced significantly higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality following IHD-diagnosis compared with controls.

papers.abstract: Abstract Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells can provide cures to patients affected by certain hematologic malignancies. Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) is a major side effect of this treatment, yet its pathophysiology remains incompletely understood and selective therapeutic options are limited. In this issue, Li and colleagues identify the CCR1–CCR2 axis as a key mediator of inflammatory macrophage recruitment to sites of CAR T-cell activation, thereby contributing to CRS. In preclinical models, blockade of this axis prevented macrophage recruitment and substantially diminished CRS severity. This discovery could open a new avenue for targeted intervention against CRS, although further validation of the role of the CCR1/CCR2 axis, particularly in clinically relevant settings, is required. papers.abstract: Abstract To date, non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide, underscoring the urgent need for new treatment options. The oncofetal carbohydrate CD176 is masked on healthy tissues but is present on a variety of cancer entities and is associated with cancer invasiveness and metastasis. In this study, we employed chimeric antigen receptor T cells (CAR-T) directed against CD176 for treatment of NSCLC. CD176-CAR-Ts were optimized with an additional inducible cassette encoding IL18 (CD176-iIL18-TRUCK) or IL12 (CD176-iIL12-TRUCK) to augment antitumor reactivity through autocrine and paracrine signaling. CD176-iIL18- and CD176-iIL12-TRUCKs eradicated NSCLC cells in a three-dimensional tumor spheroid model and tissue slices derived from patients with lung adenocarcinoma more potently than CD176-CAR-Ts. Administration of TRUCKs in a lung carcinoma xenograft mouse model resulted in partial or complete tumor eradication in all mice treated with CD176-iIL12-TRUCKs and in 50% of mice treated with CD176-iIL18-TRUCKs. This study highlights the potential of CD176 as a CAR T-cell target and suggests CD176-CAR-Ts armored with IL18 or IL12 as a promising new therapeutic approach for the treatment of NSCLC and several other CD176-positive cancer entities.

papers.abstract: Background: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are common toxicities of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but their prognostic implications in older adults remain uncertain. Patients and Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using SEER–Medicare (2010–2019). We included patients aged ≥66 years with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC who initiated ICI monotherapy or chemoimmunotherapy from 2015–2017. Follow-up began at treatment initiation and continued until death, Medicare disenrollment, or December 31, 2019. The primary exposure was a clinically meaningful irAE, defined as an irAE diagnosis with evidence of systemic immunosuppressant use and/or treatment delay, or discontinuation. In secondary analyses, we categorized patients as having no irAE, an irAE managed without hospitalization, or an irAE requiring hospitalization. The primary outcome was overall survival. We estimated adjusted survival differences and restricted mean survival time using doubly robust causal inference methods. Results: The cohort included 5,304 patients (mean age, 75 years; 52.7% female; 81.9% White). Clinically meaningful irAEs occurred in 1,807 (34.1%) patients, with a median onset of 3.8 months (IQR, 1.1–9.4). Death occurred in 65.1% of patients with irAEs and 78.7% without irAEs, corresponding to an adjusted absolute survival benefit of 6.6% (95% CI, 5.3%–8.0%) and a 6.5-month gain in restricted mean survival time (95% CI, 5.6–7.4). In secondary analyses, irAEs managed without hospitalization showed the greatest benefit (odds ratio [OR], 0.44; 95% CI, 0.35–0.54), whereas irAE hospitalization was associated with attenuated benefit (OR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89–0.99). Conclusions: Among older adults with advanced NSCLC receiving ICIs, clinically meaningful irAEs were associated with improved overall survival, particularly when managed without hospitalization. These findings highlight the clinical importance of early recognition of immune-related toxicities; irAE-related hospitalization may identify a higher-risk group warranting closer monitoring and supportive care.

papers.abstract: Abstract Cancer immunotherapies have achieved meaningful clinical benefits but remain limited by systemic toxicities that restrict the use of potent immune modulators. CD47-targeting antibodies promote tumor cell phagocytosis but are hindered by hematologic toxicity, whereas IL2 activates cytotoxic lymphocytes but induces broad, dose-limiting immune activation. In this study, we engineered a reciprocally masked antibody–cytokine fusion [CD47-specific antibody (aCD47)/IL2/IL2 receptor complex (IL2c)] designed for tumor-selective activation. In this construct, an aCD47 and an IL2c sterically and functionally suppress each other via protease-cleavable linkers, preventing CD47 blockade and IL2 receptor engagement in circulation while enabling protease-dependent unmasking within the tumor microenvironment. A human construct demonstrated masking and protease-dependent restoration of both CD47–signal regulatory protein alpha (SIRPα) blockade and IL2 signaling, with improved systemic tolerability in human CD47/SIRPα transgenic mice, supporting translational potential. A murine analog enabled mechanistic and efficacy studies in immunocompetent tumor models. The tolerability of mouse aCD47/IL2c was improved in comparison with individual components. Antitumor activity required both CD47 blockade and IL2 activity and resulted in robust antitumor efficacy, including in an immune checkpoint–resistant melanoma model. The robust antitumor efficacy was associated with inflammatory macrophage polarization and increased numbers of effector CD8+ T cells inside the tumor. Unlike conventional CD47 antibodies or IL2 therapies, this approach enabled coordinated, tumor-localized activation of innate and adaptive immunity while limiting systemic exposure. Together, these data highlight reciprocal masking as a clinically relevant strategy to expand the therapeutic index of immune modulators constrained by systemic toxicity.

papers.abstract: Abstract Histone lactylation is an epigenetic modification that connects lactate metabolism with protein function. Our study identified that lactate enhances the protein lactylation level not only in the myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSC) of tumor-bearing mice but also in the tumor tissues of patients with lung cancer. This modification led to the upregulation of CD38 expression and enhanced the immunosuppressive function of MDSCs. Mechanistically, CD38 promoted immunosuppression by depleting NAD+, and treatment with a CD38 inhibitor or siRNA-mediated knockdown of CD38 in MDSCs delayed tumor progression. Histone H3 lysine 18 is enriched at the CD38 promoter region, with p300, histone deacetylases 1 to 3, and bromodomain-containing protein 4 identified as key epigenetic regulators in this process. Our findings reveal the critical role of the lactate–CD38–NAD+ axis in regulating MDSC immunosuppressive function and establish histone lactylation as an epigenetic mechanism controlling CD38 expression.

papers.abstract: Abstract The spatial arrangement of immune cells in the tumor microenvironment (TME) varies widely, from dispersed to clustered and tumor-excluded to infiltrating. Multiplexed spatial profiling is an effective means of characterizing tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and immune complexes such as tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) in the TME. However, few approaches have been described for objectively parametrizing patterns of immune organization and assessing their association with biological or clinical variables. This makes it difficult to evaluate whether a set of tumors is relatively immunologically cold or hot. In this study, we describe an intuitive set of statistical tools (available in the R package, tlsR) for characterizing lymphocyte patterns in the TME of solid cancers. We applied tlsR to primary prostate cancer, which is often described as immunologically “cold.” Using a cohort of 29 radical prostatectomy specimens stratified into low Gleason grade (LGG; n = 15) and high Gleason grade (HGG; n = 14), we showed that HGG prostate cancer is significantly more infiltrated than LGG prostate cancer, with lymphocytes organized into B or T cell–enriched immune clusters (IC). A subset of these ICs had the B- and T-cell zonation and follicular dendritic cells characteristic of bona fide TLSs. HGGs were also enriched with ICs containing precursors of exhausted T cells and proliferating B cells, and their tumor compartments harbored granzyme B+ cytotoxic T cells in contact with cancer cells. Thus, far from being cold, a subset of HGG prostate cancer has features associated with active immune surveillance, a finding with implications for emerging prostate cancer immunotherapies.

papers.abstract: The efficacy of immunotherapy is commonly increased by simultaneous anti‐angiogenesis treatment. An experimental breast cancer model exhibits vascular normalization with reduced vascular leakage when grown in mice with endothelial Shb deficiency. This mutant ablates the effects of vascular endothelial growth factor A on angiogenesis and leakage. Unexpectedly, the endothelial gene expression changes that were observed under these conditions suggested an immunosuppressive state. Comparison of healthy human breast endothelium with breast cancer endothelium revealed similar immune suppressive gene expression differences, and lung cancer and colorectal cancer showed analogous patterns of changes. These findings suggest that normalized or physiologically normal endothelium may have immunosuppressive features, with implications for the optimization of cancer immunotherapy regimens.

papers.abstract: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma is a common skin malignancy in aging populations. Surgical resection and radiotherapy can result in significant morbidity, as well as functional and cosmetic impairments. PD-1 antibodies are promising treatments for locally advanced disease. Two elderly men (aged 71 and 73) with locoregionally advanced head and neck tumors received neoadjuvant treatment with cemiplimab (350 mg IV every 3 weeks). Both patients presented with neurologic symptoms concerning for nerve involvement; however, perineural spread could not be identified radiographically or by limited biopsies. Both patients achieved a significant clinical response after only four doses of cemiplimab. After 4 additional doses, both patients underwent elective treatment discontinuation and surgery and radiotherapy were omitted. With over 12-month follow-up, both patients remained free of recurrence. Treatment was well-tolerated with only Grade 1 pruritus. These observations are promising and suggest the feasibility of response-adapted management following cemiplimab therapy in selected patients with advanced squamous cell skin cancer with resolution of neurologic symptoms. This approach may allow for omission of surgery and radiotherapy in selected patients. Further investigation to define appropriate candidates for this approach appears warranted.

papers.abstract: Serum free light chain (sFLC) testing is central to the diagnosis and monitoring of plasma cell disorders, but assay availability and implementation can vary by laboratory setting. We evaluated a domestic latex-enhanced immunoturbidimetric Kehua serum sFLC assay against Freelite and N Latex systems. Residual serum samples from 133 adults with suspected or established monoclonal gammopathies were measured in parallel by Kehua and Freelite; 122 were also tested by N Latex. Precision was assessed with low- and high-level serum controls. Method agreement was evaluated using correlation, Passing-Bablok regression, Bland-Altman analysis, qualitative concordance and comparator-defined ROC analysis. Kehua within-run CVs were <5% for κ and λ controls. Agreement with Freelite was excellent for FLC-κ, FLC-λ and κ/λ ratio (Pearson r = 0.988-1.000; CCC = 0.983-0.999), with Passing-Bablok slopes close to unity. Agreement with N Latex was also strong (r = 0.991-0.998), although κ/λ ratio showed proportional bias. Total qualitative concordance was 89.47-93.23% versus Freelite and 83.61-91.80% versus N Latex, with Cohen's κ of 0.67-0.85. Comparator-defined ROC AUCs were 0.994-0.999 for elevated FLC-κ or FLC-λ and 0.796-0.869 for κ/λ ratio abnormality. The Kehua serum assay demonstrated acceptable precision and good clinical agreement with two imported methods. It may serve as a domestic option for routine serum sFLC quantification, provided method-specific intervals are maintained and the same platform is used for serial monitoring.

papers.abstract: Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) has undergone substantial epidemiological and clinical changes, with an increasing proportion of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated tumours and declining tobacco exposure. We investigated temporal changes in patient characteristics, HPV/p16 status, treatment patterns, and survival among patients with OPSCC in Denmark. Patients with OPSCC were identified from the Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database (2000-2023) and the Danish National Patient Cancer Registry (DCR; 1980-2021). The Copenhagen database provided detailed clinical and pathological data, including HPV/p16 status, while the DCR enabled assessment of long-term survival trends. Temporal changes were evaluated across diagnostic periods. Overall survival, relative survival, and restricted mean survival time were estimated. Among 3,631 OPSCC patients in the Copenhagen database, median age at diagnosis increased from 59 years in 2000-2005 to 64 years in 2018-2023 (p<0.001). The proportion of HPV+/p16+ patients increased significantly from 43.5% in 2000-2005 to 62.8% in 2018-2023. The proportion of never smokers also increased from 0.5% to 23.5%, while ≥20 pack-years decreased from 73.2% to 52.1% (p<0.001). Treatment patterns changed substantially, with radiotherapy alone decreasing from 87.6% to 27.9% and chemoradiotherapy increasing from 1.6% to 46.3%. Among 9,379 patients in the DCR, five-year relative survival increased from 31.8% in 1980-1984 to 70.1% in 2015-2019. Among HPV+/p16+ patients, five-year overall survival increased from 63.1% in 2000-2005 to 83.7% in 2018-2023. In Denmark, OPSCC has undergone substantial epidemiological and therapeutic changes accompanied by marked improvements in survival, including among HPV+/p16+ patients.

papers.abstract: Frailty and low handgrip strength are established markers of limited physiological reserve, but it is uncertain whether their prognostic meaning differs between oncologic and non-oncologic surgery. We examined whether oncologic indication modifies the associations of preoperative frailty and baseline handgrip strength with early postoperative outcomes. This secondary analysis used a prospective cohort conducted at participating surgical centers between January 2023 and June 2025. Frailty was classified using the Fried phenotype, and handgrip strength was measured at admission. The primary outcome was prolonged length of stay (LOS >10 days); secondary outcomes were any postoperative complication, major complications, and log-transformed LOS. Effect modification was evaluated using interaction terms in multivariable logistic models adjusted for age and sex. Because no prolonged stays occurred among fit patients in the non-oncologic stratum, categorical frailty models used Firth penalized logistic regression. Among 222 clinically characterized participants, 118 (53.2%) underwent oncologic surgery. Prolonged LOS occurred in 41/118 (34.7%) oncologic and 7/104 (6.7%) non-oncologic patients. The complete-case primary analysis included 216 patients and 45 events. In an additional ordinal main-effects model, increasing frailty [odds ratio (OR) 2.91 per category, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.57-5.38], lower handgrip strength (OR 0.95 per kg, 95% CI 0.90-0.99), and oncologic indication (OR 8.97, 95% CI 3.47-23.19) were associated with prolonged LOS. However, categorical frailty-by-oncology interaction was not supported (global p = 0.341), nor was handgrip-strength-by-oncology interaction (p = 0.739); the joint interaction test was not statistically significant (p = 0.525). No convincing effect modification was observed for complications or continuous LOS. Oncologic surgery was associated with a substantially higher early postoperative burden, while frailty and handgrip strength retained prognostic relevance. No clear evidence of multiplicative interaction by oncologic indication was detected, but clinically meaningful effect modification cannot be excluded. Physiological reserve assessment should therefore be considered across elective abdominal surgery rather than restricted to the oncologic setting.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are increasingly used as bridging or downstaging therapy before liver transplantation (LT) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but biomarkers of posttransplant recurrence in this setting are lacking. We evaluated the association between pretransplant plasma soluble programmed death-1 (sPD-1) and posttransplant outcomes after pretransplant ICI therapy. We enrolled 105 HCC patients undergoing LT, including 51 receiving ICIs and 54 without prior ICI exposure. Pretransplant plasma sPD-1 and sPD-L1 were measured by ELISA. The primary endpoint was 2-year recurrence-free survival (RFS). Associations were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression. Pretransplant sPD-1 was higher in the ICI group than in the non-ICI group (P < 0.0001). Within the ICI-treated cohort, patients who experienced recurrence had higher sPD-1 than those who did not (P = 0.0002), whereas sPD-L1 did not differ. At an internally derived exploratory cutoff of 2073 pg/mL, high sPD-1 was associated with lower 2-year RFS (7.7% vs. 76.3%; log-rank P < 0.0001; HR, 4.42; 95% CI, 1.75-11.17). As a continuous variable, each doubling of pretransplant sPD-1 was associated with an increased risk of recurrence in the unadjusted analysis (HR = 1.51, 95% CI 1.25-1.82; P < 0.001). The association remained significant after adjustment for AFP, tumor number, and maximum tumor diameter (adjusted HR = 1.51, 95% CI 1.20-1.89; P < 0.001). Elevated pretransplant sPD-1 is independently associated with increased posttransplant recurrence risk in HCC patients receiving ICIs before LT. This association remained after adjustment for AFP and pretransplant tumor burden, and appeared distinct from MVI status, ACR occurrence, and the timing of blood sampling. sPD-1 may serve as a complementary biomarker for risk stratification, but external validation is required.

papers.abstract: Human tumor-associated microbes - the tumor microbiome - have demonstrated an increasingly important role in human health due to their relevance to cancer progression and treatment response. While the metabolism at the host-microbiota interface, such as in the human gut, has been extensively investigated in recent years, the specialized metabolites from the tumor microbiome remain uncharted territory. To address this knowledge gap, we report a survey of the biosynthetic potential of the human tumor microbiome. Utilizing high-quality microbial metagenome-assembled genomes from 3,526 human tumor tissue samples, we identify 528 biosynthetic gene clusters with the potential to encode specialized metabolites relevant to tumor pathology. We reveal that the tumor microbiome encodes known and unknown metabolites spanning multiple biosynthetic classes. From this diverse biosynthetic landscape, we express a conserved family of biosynthetic genes from the genus Fusobacterium, which has a well-established role in cancer, and discover distinct families of long-chain fatty acyl amides. We subsequently find that one of these fatty acyl amides, oleoyl γ-aminobutyric acid, has immunomodulatory and G-protein-coupled receptor partial agonist activities, potentially supporting the influence of Fusobacterium in tumor pathology. The findings of our investigation lay a foundation for further research into the roles of tumor microbe-derived metabolites in cancer.
